coatingPage.title: Ceramic coating
coatingPage.intro: A hard, clear layer over the paint that water and dirt don't hold on to.

photo.alt: A black coupé's headlight and wing, the studio lights reflected in the paint

body: We correct the paint first: a coating locks in whatever is underneath, swirls included.
It cures for about a week. After that a normal two-bucket wash is all it needs, with a top-up at six months.

filmPage.title: Paint protection film
filmPage.intro: Clear film over the paint where stones, scuffs and car parks reach it.
body: We cut each panel's film to fit and wrap the edges where the panel allows, so it's hard to see.
Under it, the paint is corrected first: film keeps what's underneath, good or bad.

items.title: Washing a coated car
items.line: Two buckets, one mitt, and nothing that brushes.

photo.alt: A folded grey microfibre cloth on a gloss black bonnet beside the headlight

body: A coating makes washing easier, not unnecessary. Dirt that sits on it still scratches when it's dragged across.
Rinse first, from the top, to lift what you can without touching it. Then one bucket of shampoo, one of clean water for the mitt, and straight lines, not circles.
Dry with a clean towel or blown air. Skip the automatic wash: the brushes put back what we took out.

items.title: Film or coating?
items.line: One stops stones. The other makes the rest easy.

photo.alt: A car in the bay with clear film laid over the bonnet and wings, mid-fit

body: Film is a physical layer. It takes a stone chip so the paint doesn't. A coating is far thinner: it's about water, dirt and gloss.
Most of our cars get both: film on the front, where the stones hit, and a coating over everything, film included.

items.title: Winter care

photo.alt: Water standing in tight beads on a coated grey-green panel

body: Road salt is the thing to rinse off, often, and especially under the arches.
If the car sits for weeks, wash it before it does: dirt left on paint all winter is harder to shift in spring.

Your car is the only one in the bay while it's with us. It's locked in overnight.

questions.q: How long do you keep the car?
questions.a: Each package says: one day for Enhance, three for Correct, five for Armour. We confirm when you book.
Yes, from the districts around Weybridge on set days. Check your postcode on the booking page.
Film stops stone chips; a coating keeps water and dirt off. Many cars get film on the front and a coating everywhere.
After a week. The first wash card puts the day in your calendar.
A little: that's what removes the swirls. We measure every panel first and do less where a panel can't take it.

questions.q: Where is the car while you have it?
questions.a: In our heated bay, locked in overnight. It's the only car in there.
